Problem Statement Title	
Development of an APAAR ID-Based Student Data Management and Verification Platform for AICTE-Approved Institutions
Description	
Problem Description AICTE currently receives student-related information from approved institutions through different data submission mechanisms. While PGDM institutions provide detailed student data annually, other AICTE-approved institutions primarily provide statistical information such as total enrolment during the approval process. This creates challenges in maintaining complete, authentic, and verifiable student records. With APAAR ID serving as a national academic identity, there is a need to develop an integrated digital platform that uses APAAR ID as a unique academic identifier for students enrolled in AICTE-approved institutions. The proposed solution should enable institutions to securely submit student-level data to the AICTE portal after the completion of admissions and facilitate real-time verification and monitoring of student records. Key Requirements 1. Develop a secure platform/API through which AICTE-approved institutions can upload and update student-level information using APAAR ID as the unique identifier. 2. Provide data fields for: o Approved Intake o Actual Student Enrolment o Supernumerary Seats o NRI Category o OCI Status o Foreign National (FN) Status o Other relevant student information. 3. Provide automated validation to identify: o Duplicate student records o Invalid/missing APAAR IDs o Admissions exceeding approved intake o Inconsistencies in student data o Potential duplicate enrolment across institutions. 4. Develop dashboards for AICTE and institutions for monitoring admissions and student records in real time. 5. Provide a secure verification mechanism for authorized stakeholders such as AICTE, institutions, employers, and other regulatory bodies. 6. Enable generation of verifiable student records linked to the student's academic identity. 7. Provide integration/API capability with existing institutional and AICTE systems. 8. Ensure appropriate data security, privacy, authentication, role-based access control, audit trails, and consent mechanisms. 9. Enable generation of reports for policy-making, accreditation, monitoring, and regulatory purposes. 10. Support printing/display of APAAR ID along with the student ID on certificates issued by degree-awarding bodies. Expected Solution Participants are expected to develop a scalable, secure, interoperable and user-friendly APAAR-based Student Data Management and Verification System that can be integrated with the AICTE portal. The solution should provide: Institution → Student Data Upload → APAAR Validation → Data Verification → AICTE Central Repository → Analytics & Monitoring → Authorized Verification Expected Outcome The proposed solution should enable AICTE to establish authentic and verifiable student records linked to a national academic identity, facilitate real-time monitoring of admissions, detect excess enrolment, and strengthen data-driven governance and policy formulation. Innovation Expected The solution should go beyond simple data collection by providing automated validation, intelligent anomaly detection, real-time monitoring, secure verification, and analytics, thereby creating a reliable national-level student data ecosystem for AICTE-approved institutions.

I updated the report to match the full problem statement. Requirements 5 to 10 change the plan, and my first version had left out part of what they ask for.

**What changed**
- **Requirements 5 to 10:** these ask for secure verification for AICTE, institutions, employers and regulators, and for verifiable student records. They also ask for consent and audit trails, reports, and the APAAR ID printed on certificates. I had parked the signed-record and selective-disclosure work from your v2 as "roadmap only". It is now a core module, narrowed to enrolment and identity records rather than marksheets.
- **Scope decisions:** forensics, OCR and credit transfer stay out because nothing in the statement asks for them.
- **Verification (section 10):** a bare APAAR ID never returns data, since it will be printed on certificates. Each verifier sees only what its role and the student's consent allow, as a signed record with a tick-by-tick verification receipt.
- **Certificates:** a certificate stamp that returns the APAAR ID next to the student ID plus a QR token, and a check on certificate lists. Certificates come from degree-awarding bodies, mostly universities, so the plan covers them too.
- **Innovation clause:** anomaly detection is now layered and explainable instead of a bare Isolation Forest. It uses peer benchmarking, change-point detection, outlier scoring with reasons, and a fixed review budget. Dashboards update live.
- **Integration and reports:** the integration approach (OpenAPI, signed webhooks, SFTP drop, adapters behind interfaces) and a report catalog with snapshot IDs and small-count suppression are both in the doc.
- **Plan and demo:** the 36-hour plan, team roles, demo (now 5 minutes), idea PPT outline and open questions are all updated. The plan now has a cut line for what to drop if you fall behind.

I built the working engine core (milestone M0) and wrote the playbook for everything after it. Everything below was measured in my sandbox, so re-run it on your machine.

APAAR verification uses a mock behind an interface, as you decided. A real adapter can replace it later without touching the validation code.

**What the engine does today**
- **Rules as data:** 32 rules live in `rules/ay_2026_27.yaml`, each with a severity, a handbook clause reference and fix text. Changing a cap or a severity is a YAML edit plus a test.
- **Validation:** it checks schema, APAAR IDs, duplicates, capacity and cross-field logic. It also reconciles declared totals against the student rows and detects cross-institution overlap.
- **Over-admission handling:** it implements your worked cases A to E, including the vacant-seat exception. Case D is a warning rather than a false alarm.
- **Cross-institution privacy:** an institution sees only "another active enrolment exists", while AICTE sees the full case.
- **Submission workflow:** a second person must approve certification. The result is a signed receipt, and tampering with the audit log or the receipt is detected.
- **Tests:** 37 tests pass. The engine validates about 145,000 rows in 7 seconds (about 21,000 rows per second, single thread, in memory).

**Read the 1.00 accuracy score with care.** I wrote both the data generator and the rules, so a perfect score only shows the engine does what I specified. It does not show the rules match AICTE's handbook. Several cap values come from news reports and secondary sources, and the assumptions register lists each one for you to verify.

The playbook covers the workflow, the process rules I will enforce, milestones M1 to M8 with exit criteria and hours, the learning order, a risk register and a cut line for the finale. The rules that keep the project flexible are in the repo's `docs/PROCESS.md`.
